questions.stem: A Massachusetts-licensed health care facility has no on-site pharmacy. Its outside pharmacy provider wants to place an automated dispensing device (ADD) in a patient-care area. Before the ADD is used, what is the best compliance step?

choices.text: Use it once the pharmacy owns every medication loaded into the cabinet.
Obtain approval for the ADD's use and placement from the facility's licensing body.
Obtain only a new wholesaler permit for the outside pharmacy.
Begin use after the pharmacy's manager of record signs an internal memo.
Delay approval until the first Schedule II medication is stocked.

explanation.core_reasoning: A facility without an on-site pharmacy needs licensing-body approval for ADD use and placement.

choice_analysis.A: Ownership does not replace facility approval.
choice_analysis.B: Policy requires licensing-body approval.
choice_analysis.C: A wholesaler permit is not the stated approval.
choice_analysis.D: Internal approval alone is insufficient.
choice_analysis.E: Approval is not triggered only by C-II stock.

related_facts: The ADD policy applies to Massachusetts-licensed health care facilities.
explanation.mpje_trap: Confusing pharmacy ownership of stock with facility authorization.

reasoning_steps: Identify that the facility lacks an on-site pharmacy
Apply the ADD facility-approval condition

questions.stem: A hospital unit receives a pharmacy-supplied ADD containing several patient-care medications. A nurse asks whether the facility owns the medications once they are loaded into the cabinet. Under the Massachusetts ADD policy, which answer is most accurate?

choices.text: The facility owns them immediately when the ADD door is closed.
The nurse owns custody of them after the first cabinet login.
The pharmacy retains ownership until the medication is dispensed for administration.
The patient owns every dose as soon as an order is entered.
Ownership transfers to the wholesaler whenever a dose is returned.

explanation.core_reasoning: Medication in the ADD remains pharmacy property until dispensed for administration.

choice_analysis.A: Loading does not transfer ownership.
choice_analysis.B: Access is not ownership.
choice_analysis.C: That is the policy's ownership point.
choice_analysis.D: An order alone does not transfer ADD ownership.
choice_analysis.E: The wholesaler is not the default owner.

related_facts: Facility access and pharmacy ownership are separate concepts.
explanation.mpje_trap: Treating physical custody as legal ownership.

reasoning_steps: Identify ADD stock before dispensing
Locate the policy's ownership-transfer point

questions.stem: A patient is admitted to a Massachusetts facility with an ADD. The cabinet contains the requested medication, but no valid patient-specific prescription or medication order has yet been entered. What should occur?

choices.text: Remove a dose because presence in the ADD itself authorizes administration.
Use the dose if a technician verbally confirms the usual regimen.
Wait for a valid patient-specific prescription or order before dispensing the medication from the ADD.
Treat every ADD item as floor stock that needs no patient-specific authorization.
Dispense now and obtain the order only if a controlled substance was selected.

explanation.core_reasoning: ADD availability does not substitute for a valid patient-specific prescription or order.

choice_analysis.A: Stocking is not dispensing authority.
choice_analysis.B: Technician confirmation is not a valid order.
choice_analysis.C: A valid patient-specific order is required.
choice_analysis.D: The policy does not create blanket floor-stock authority.
choice_analysis.E: The order condition is not limited to federal controls.

related_facts: The device stores medication; it does not create prescriptive authority.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming stocked medication is automatically authorized for a patient.

reasoning_steps: Separate cabinet inventory from dispensing authority
Require the patient-specific prescription or order

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy audits its ADD program. Which records or data should be retained as part of the ADD record system? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A verbal recollection from the charge nurse instead of a retrievable transaction record
Documentation of required approval for the ADD location
ADD transaction data showing product, patient identifier, date/time, and reconciliation
Records of ADD maintenance and personnel access/events
Retain retrievable ADD records for at least two years as required by the device policy.

explanation.core_reasoning: ADD records include approvals, device/event information, access, transaction details, and reconciliation rather than a single purchase record.

choice_analysis.A: Verbal recollection is not the required record.
choice_analysis.B: Approval documentation belongs in the record set.
choice_analysis.C: Transaction and reconciliation data are required.
choice_analysis.D: Maintenance and access events are tracked.
choice_analysis.E: The ADD policy requires retention of the device records for at least two years.

related_facts: The pharmacy maintains ADD records for at least two years under the policy.
explanation.mpje_trap: Substituting ordinary purchasing records for ADD accountability records.

reasoning_steps: Identify ADD-specific record categories
Reject substitutes that omit device-event accountability

questions.stem: A pharmacy is preparing medications for an ADD at a Massachusetts health care facility. Which actions are consistent with the current ADD policy? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Load a manufacturer's sealed original single-dose package when suitable
Use medication repackaged according to professional standards for a single dose or person
Report medication losses according to the pharmacy licensing body's requirements
Use single-dose or person-specific packaging that preserves medication identity and traceability.
Ignore a documented shortage if all missing doses are Schedule VI

explanation.core_reasoning: ADD stock must preserve appropriate package integrity and medication losses remain reportable under applicable licensing requirements.

choice_analysis.A: Sealed original packaging is acceptable.
choice_analysis.B: Proper single-dose/person repackaging is permitted.
choice_analysis.C: Loss reporting follows licensing-body requirements.
choice_analysis.D: Appropriate single-dose/person packaging supports ADD product integrity and traceability.
choice_analysis.E: Schedule VI status does not erase accountability.

related_facts: Single-dose/person packaging supports traceability.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming lower schedules eliminate device accountability.

reasoning_steps: Classify acceptable ADD package presentation
Apply loss-accountability requirements

questions.stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy uses one ADD only as an approved emergency medication kit and a second ADD for routine medication dispensing. A licensed nurse asks to load both machines. Which answer best applies under the current ADD policy?

choices.text: The nurse may load the emergency-kit ADD; routine-dispensing ADD loading is limited to certified technicians or interns under pharmacist supervision.
The nurse may load both machines because the same pharmacy owns both devices and supervises the medication inventory.
The nurse may load neither machine because routine and emergency ADDs are restricted to pharmacists and pharmacy interns.
The nurse may load the routine machine whenever it contains only Schedule VI medications and no federally controlled drugs.
Both machines use the emergency-kit loader list as long as they are located inside the same Massachusetts retail pharmacy.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts distinguishes emergency-kit ADD loading from routine retail ADD loading; licensed nurses are listed for the former, while the latter uses supervised certified-technician or intern loading.

choice_analysis.A: The policy uses a broader loader list for emergency-kit use and a narrower supervised loader pathway for routine retail dispensing.
choice_analysis.B: Common ownership does not make the two ADD purposes follow the same loader rule.
choice_analysis.C: A licensed nurse is an authorized loader for the emergency-kit pathway.
choice_analysis.D: Limiting inventory to Schedule VI does not broaden the routine-dispensing loader list.
choice_analysis.E: The device's approved purpose, not merely location, determines the applicable loading pathway.

related_facts: Routine retail ADDs also carry machine-specific registration and continuous-video requirements.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming one authorized emergency-kit loader automatically has the same authority for routine dispensing.

reasoning_steps: Classify each ADD by emergency-kit versus routine-dispensing use
Apply the distinct loader rule for each mode

questions.stem: A retail pharmacy plans to use an ADD for routine medication dispensing rather than only as an emergency kit. Which controls apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Have it loaded by a certified pharmacy technician or pharmacy intern under Massachusetts pharmacist supervision
Maintain transaction and reconciliation records for the routine ADD program.
Treat the machine as exempt from pharmacy policies because it is computer controlled
Obtain a machine-specific DEA registration and Controlled Substance Registration as required by the policy
Continuously monitor the ADD by video

explanation.core_reasoning: Routine retail ADD dispensing adds machine-specific registration, continuous video, and credentialed supervised loading requirements.

choice_analysis.A: Those are the listed routine loaders.
choice_analysis.B: Routine ADD use remains subject to device transaction and reconciliation accountability.
choice_analysis.C: ADD use remains subject to policies and law.
choice_analysis.D: Routine retail ADD use carries machine-specific registrations.
choice_analysis.E: Continuous video monitoring is required.

related_facts: General ADD safety, security, and accountability duties still apply.
explanation.mpje_trap: Importing the broader emergency-kit loader list into routine dispensing.

reasoning_steps: Distinguish routine retail dispensing from emergency-kit use
Apply machine registration, monitoring, and loader requirements

questions.stem: A pharmacy technician trainee is assigned to restock an ADD at a satellite Massachusetts clinic. The clinic is licensed, but it has no on-site pharmacy and the ADD address is different from the pharmacy's MCSR address. Can the trainee use the special 2023 ADD-stocking pathway?

choices.text: Yes; trainee status is enough when the clinic is licensed and the pharmacist provides remote direction.
Yes; limiting the cabinet to Schedule VI removes the location conditions for trainee stocking.
No; the pathway requires an on-site pharmacy and an ADD at the same physical address listed on the facility MCSR.
No; trainees may work with ADD inventory only after becoming nationally certified technicians.
Yes; a personal DEA registration for the trainee would substitute for the facility-location conditions.

explanation.core_reasoning: The PTT ADD pathway is location-limited and cannot be used at the described off-site clinic.

choice_analysis.A: Facility prerequisites still apply to the trainee pathway.
choice_analysis.B: Schedule does not replace the facility-location requirements.
choice_analysis.C: Both required location conditions are missing in the scenario.
choice_analysis.D: Eligible trainees have a defined stocking pathway without national certification.
choice_analysis.E: A personal DEA registration does not cure the facility-location defect.

related_facts: The pharmacy must also maintain policies and training for the permitted activities.
explanation.mpje_trap: Checking only schedule or credential while ignoring facility prerequisites.

reasoning_steps: Identify the special technician-stocking policy
Check on-site pharmacy and MCSR-address prerequisites

questions.stem: At an eligible hospital ADD, a pharmacy technician trainee works under pharmacist direction and supervision but without direct pharmacist supervision. Which tasks may the trainee perform under the Massachusetts ADD stocking policy? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Override a clinical interaction warning before the dose is released
Transport and load pharmacist-verified Schedule III-VI stock using barcode or other electronic validation
Verify expiration dates and remove expired Schedule III-VI stock using electronic validation
Load an unverified Schedule IV bottle based only on the trainee's visual check
Transport and load Schedule II stock under the PTT pathway

explanation.core_reasoning: A PTT may perform defined pharmacist-verified Schedule III-VI inventory functions, not C-II or clinical judgment tasks.

choice_analysis.A: Clinical judgment is outside this inventory exception.
choice_analysis.B: This is an expressly permitted PTT function.
choice_analysis.C: Expired-stock removal is permitted.
choice_analysis.D: PTT loading requires pharmacist-verified stock.
choice_analysis.E: PTT stocking is limited to III-VI.

related_facts: The activity remains under pharmacist direction and supervision.
explanation.mpje_trap: Equating absence of direct supervision with independent practice.

reasoning_steps: Identify trainee rather than licensed-technician privileges
Apply verification, schedule, and electronic-validation conditions

questions.stem: A nationally certified Massachusetts-licensed pharmacy technician is using the special ADD stocking pathway without prior pharmacist verification. Which conditions must be satisfied? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The medication is non-patient-specific Schedule VI stock
The medication is not a PMP drug such as gabapentin
Barcode scanning or other electronic validation is used
Transfer qualifying stock in manufacturer-sealed or original packaging without further manipulation.
The same no-prior-verification shortcut extends to Schedule V because the technician is nationally certified

explanation.core_reasoning: The no-prior-verification shortcut is narrowly limited to nonpatient-specific, non-PMP Schedule VI stock transferred without further manipulation using electronic validation.

choice_analysis.A: The shortcut is limited to nonpatient-specific S-VI.
choice_analysis.B: PMP drugs are excluded from this shortcut.
choice_analysis.C: Electronic validation is part of the pathway.
choice_analysis.D: The no-prior-verification shortcut requires qualifying stock to be transferred without further manipulation.
choice_analysis.E: The pathway is Schedule VI only.

related_facts: Manufacturer-sealed original packaging is an example of no further manipulation.
explanation.mpje_trap: Treating national certification as authority to bypass schedule or PMP limits.

reasoning_steps: Identify nationally certified licensed technician status
Apply Schedule VI, PMP, packaging, and electronic-validation limits
Reject broader technician privileges

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a prescription marked 'EPT' for the untreated sex partner of a patient diagnosed with gonorrhea but not chlamydia. The prescription otherwise appears valid. Under the Board/DCP EPT dispensing policy, what is the key issue?

choices.text: The cited pharmacy EPT policy covers gonorrhea and chlamydia whenever the partner has not been examined.
It does not fit; the cited Massachusetts pharmacy EPT policy is limited to chlamydia treatment.
It fits only when gonorrhea is treated with a federally controlled antibiotic.
It fits when the prescription is electronic, even though the diagnosis is gonorrhea alone.
It fits after the partner gives the pharmacy identifying information, regardless of diagnosis.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts pharmacy EPT dispensing policy applies only to chlamydia treatment.

choice_analysis.A: The cited Massachusetts pharmacy EPT policy is not a general STI pathway.
choice_analysis.B: The diagnosis in the scenario is outside the policy's chlamydia scope.
choice_analysis.C: Federal controlled-substance status is not the EPT eligibility criterion.
choice_analysis.D: Prescription format does not expand the policy's diagnosis scope.
choice_analysis.E: Providing identity information does not convert gonorrhea-only treatment into this EPT pathway.

related_facts: EPT treats a partner without examination or testing under this policy.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming one EPT process automatically covers every STI.

reasoning_steps: Identify the diagnosed infection
Apply the chlamydia-only EPT policy scope

questions.stem: A prescriber is issuing separate Massachusetts EPT prescriptions for partners of a patient with confirmed chlamydia. Which prescription-identification approaches are acceptable under the EPT policy? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Use 'EPT' in place of the partner's name and address
Put the index patient's name on one prescription and silently dispense extra doses for unnamed partners without separate partner prescriptions
Leave all patient-identification fields blank with no EPT designation
Issue the partner prescription using the partner's actual name when known
Use 'Expedited Partner Therapy' in place of the partner's name and address

explanation.core_reasoning: The partner may be named, or an approved EPT designation may replace the partner's name and address on a separate prescription.

choice_analysis.A: The abbreviation is expressly permitted.
choice_analysis.B: The policy calls for a separate partner prescription.
choice_analysis.C: The EPT designation supplies the permitted replacement.
choice_analysis.D: A named-partner prescription is allowed.
choice_analysis.E: The full EPT designation is permitted.

related_facts: E.P.T. is also an accepted designation.
explanation.mpje_trap: Turning an identity exception into permission for a blank or combined prescription.

reasoning_steps: Confirm chlamydia EPT context
Classify each partner-identification route independently

questions.stem: A valid chlamydia-partner prescription uses 'EPT' instead of a partner name and address. The pharmacist decides to fill it. How should the pharmacy handle the patient profile and prescription label?

choices.text: Create the profile and label using the EPT designation in place of the partner's name and address.
Use the index patient's profile and label so no new record exists.
Use the prescriber's name as the patient identifier.
Dispense with no patient profile because EPT prescriptions are exempt from pharmacy records.
Invent a fictitious first and last name for the partner.

explanation.core_reasoning: The pharmacy creates a separate profile and label using an approved EPT designation.

choice_analysis.A: That is the instructed anonymous EPT workflow.
choice_analysis.B: The partner prescription gets its own EPT record.
choice_analysis.C: The prescriber does not replace the partner identifier.
choice_analysis.D: The policy instructs creation of a profile.
choice_analysis.E: The EPT designation is the permitted identifier.

related_facts: Anonymous EPT does not eliminate the pharmacy record.
explanation.mpje_trap: Using the index patient's identity for the partner's prescription.

reasoning_steps: Recognize an anonymous but valid EPT prescription
Apply the EPT profile and label instruction

questions.stem: A pharmacist receives a valid Massachusetts chlamydia EPT prescription but is unable or unwilling to fill it. What does the Board/DCP policy direct the pharmacist to do?

choices.text: Destroy the prescription so it cannot be filled elsewhere.
Refer the patient to an alternate pharmacy.
Tell the patient that no Massachusetts pharmacy may fill EPT.
Convert the prescription to an ordinary OTC sale.
Hold it indefinitely until the original patient returns with the partner.

explanation.core_reasoning: A pharmacist who cannot or will not fill a valid EPT prescription must refer to an alternate pharmacy.

choice_analysis.A: The policy does not authorize destruction.
choice_analysis.B: Referral is the specified action.
choice_analysis.C: That misstates the policy.
choice_analysis.D: EPT status does not create OTC status.
choice_analysis.E: That defeats the referral requirement.

related_facts: The policy gives a specific continuity action rather than a dispensing mandate.
explanation.mpje_trap: Confusing permission not to fill with permission to block access.

reasoning_steps: Confirm the prescription fits EPT policy
Apply the unable/unwilling-to-fill referral duty

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is reviewing requests to administer prescribed medications. Which requests fall within current Massachusetts pharmacist-administration categories, assuming all training, prescription, and guidance conditions are satisfied? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A listed long-acting injectable antipsychotic for treatment of mental illness under prescriber direction
Extended-release naltrexone for substance use disorder under the applicable guidance
Prescribed testosterone for gender-affirming care
Any prescription-only drug for any diagnosis merely because the patient prefers pharmacy administration
A routine maintenance injection for an unrelated indication solely because the product is Massachusetts Schedule VI

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts pharmacist administration is category- and condition-specific, including covered MH/SUD therapy and prescribed testosterone for gender-affirming care.

choice_analysis.A: Mental-illness administration is an authorized category subject to guidance.
choice_analysis.B: SUD administration is an authorized category.
choice_analysis.C: Current statute expressly includes this category.
choice_analysis.D: Authority is not an unlimited administration license.
choice_analysis.E: Schedule VI status alone does not create administration authority.

related_facts: Current law also includes certain STI/HIV-related administration categories.
explanation.mpje_trap: Turning enumerated administration authority into authority for any injectable prescription.

reasoning_steps: Identify each drug/indication pair
Match it to a current pharmacist-administration category
Reject schedule-only reasoning

questions.stem: A trained Massachusetts pharmacist has Vivitrol in stock and a patient asks for an injection today. There is no patient-specific prescription or prescriber direction for this dose. What is the best action under the MH/SUD administration guidance?

choices.text: Administer because Vivitrol appears on the eligible-medication list.
Administer if the patient signs a pharmacy consent form.
Do not administer until the required patient-specific prescription/prescriber direction is in place.
Convert the stock dose into an OTC medication.
Ask a technician to select the dose and administer it independently.

explanation.core_reasoning: Listing of a medication does not eliminate the patient-specific prescription and prescriber-directed nature of administration.

choice_analysis.A: Drug eligibility does not replace patient-specific authorization.
choice_analysis.B: Consent alone does not supply prescriber direction.
choice_analysis.C: The administration pathway remains prescriber-directed.
choice_analysis.D: Administration guidance does not change prescription status.
choice_analysis.E: That does not satisfy the pharmacist/intern pathway.

related_facts: Eligible products are prescribed in single doses and available in single-dose packaging.
explanation.mpje_trap: Equating product eligibility with standing authority to inject stock.

reasoning_steps: Recognize an eligible product
Check patient-specific prescriber authorization before administration

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist administers an eligible patient-specific long-acting antipsychotic under the current MH/SUD pathway. Which workflow principles are consistent with the guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Communicate the administration information back to the prescriber as required by the pathway
Allow a cashier to perform the injection after the pharmacist verifies the prescription
Skip privacy protections because the medication treats mental illness
Use a prescribed single dose supplied in eligible single-dose packaging
Document the administration in the pharmacy's patient record

explanation.core_reasoning: Eligible MH/SUD administration remains patient-specific, documented, prescriber-connected, and subject to ordinary privacy obligations.

choice_analysis.A: Prescriber communication supports ongoing assessment.
choice_analysis.B: The administration authority is not delegated to unlicensed staff.
choice_analysis.C: Privacy duties remain applicable.
choice_analysis.D: The guidance limits eligible products to prescribed single doses/single-dose packaging.
choice_analysis.E: Administration requires accountable patient documentation.

related_facts: Prescribers must reassess therapy at clinically appropriate intervals.
explanation.mpje_trap: Treating pharmacy administration as a detached walk-in injection service.

reasoning_steps: Confirm eligible MH/SUD administration
Apply dose, record, communication, and privacy workflow

questions.stem: A Massachusetts long-term-care facility is building its controlled-substance emergency-kit formulary with its single pharmacy provider. The facility wants to include a controlled analgesic. Which framework applies?

choices.text: Any quantity is allowed if the drug is Schedule VI.
The facility selects from approved Schedule II-V analgesic choices within the bed-capacity unit limit.
Only Schedule II analgesics may be included.
Controlled analgesics are prohibited from LTC emergency kits.
The pharmacy may ignore facility policies once DPH approves the drug class.

explanation.core_reasoning: LTC facilities may select approved Schedule II-V analgesics within category limits tied to licensed bed capacity.

choice_analysis.A: The described item is a controlled analgesic in the CII-V framework.
choice_analysis.B: That is the emergency-kit framework.
choice_analysis.C: The approved category spans CII-V.
choice_analysis.D: They are expressly contemplated.
choice_analysis.E: Facility procedures and accountability remain required.

related_facts: A separate sedative/anticonvulsant category has its own cap.
explanation.mpje_trap: Treating a permitted category as either unlimited or Schedule-II-only.

reasoning_steps: Identify an LTC emergency-kit analgesic
Apply the approved CII-V category and bed-capacity framework

questions.stem: A Massachusetts LTC facility has 120 licensed beds. It wants its emergency kit to contain the maximum allowed number of Schedule II-V analgesic units. What is the current maximum for that analgesic category?

choices.text: 45 units
60 units
75 units
90 units
120 units

choice_analysis.B: That cap applies to the next lower tier.
choice_analysis.C: 101-150 beds permits 75 analgesic units.
choice_analysis.D: That cap applies above 150 beds.
choice_analysis.E: The cap is not one unit per bed.

Apply the analgesic maximum for that tier

questions.stem: Which statements correctly describe Massachusetts LTC emergency-kit safeguards? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Each Schedule II-V unit should be tamper-evident/resistant and individually packaged as a single dose
A facility may use an ADD instead of the traditional locked box when relevant requirements are met
Schedule VI emergency doses remain subject to procurement, storage, dispensing, administration, recording, and disposal controls
Schedule VI emergency stock is exempt from the facility quality-assurance process
Once a kit is approved, controlled-substance accountability policies are optional

choice_analysis.A: The circular specifies that package form.
choice_analysis.B: DPH permits ADD substitution.
choice_analysis.C: Schedule VI does not escape accountability.
choice_analysis.D: Schedule VI use is monitored by the QA/assessment committee.
choice_analysis.E: Security and accountability policies remain required.

related_facts: Facilities need not stock every allowed item or the maximum quantity.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming emergency access relaxes controlled-substance safeguards.

reasoning_steps: Separate packaging, device, and Schedule VI obligations
Evaluate each safeguard independently

questions.stem: An inpatient Massachusetts hospice asks its pharmacy provider to keep a large non-patient-specific supply of acute-use controlled medications in the onsite ADD so the facility can avoid routine pharmacy deliveries. Which statement best describes the permitted acute-use purpose?

choices.text: It is a limited bridge for timely palliation until the pharmacy can fill and deliver the full patient prescription.
It is intended to reduce routine pharmacy deliveries by functioning as standing floor stock for chronic therapy.
It is intended primarily to hold larger reserve quantities when the hospice has frequent Schedule VI use.
It is intended mainly for resuscitation drugs used during immediately life-threatening emergencies.
It transfers ordinary dispensing responsibility from the pharmacy to hospice nursing staff during off-hours.

explanation.core_reasoning: Hospice acute-use stock is a limited palliative bridge until the pharmacy can fill and deliver the full prescription.

choice_analysis.B: The pathway is not a substitute for routine chronic-medication dispensing.
choice_analysis.C: The purpose is timely acute palliation, not inventory expansion based on schedule.
choice_analysis.D: The circular addresses acute palliative needs rather than a resuscitation-only stock model.
choice_analysis.E: The pharmacy remains responsible for the dispensing system and patient-specific supply.

related_facts: The pathway uses an onsite ADD for approved Schedule II-VI categories.
explanation.mpje_trap: Turning a bridge supply into routine floor stock.

reasoning_steps: Identify the inpatient hospice acute-use pathway
Apply its bridge-supply purpose

questions.stem: A pharmacy will place an acute-use ADD inside a Massachusetts inpatient hospice. Which requirements are part of the current hospice pathway? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Continuously monitor the ADD by video
Keep medications in the hospice ADD as pharmacy property until they are dispensed.
Skip prescription reconciliation because the medications are palliative
Obtain a machine-specific Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration
Determine whether a machine-specific DEA registration is required

choice_analysis.A: Continuous video monitoring applies.
choice_analysis.B: The hospice ADD pathway preserves pharmacy ownership until dispensing.
choice_analysis.C: ADD dispensing must be reconciled with prescriptions.
choice_analysis.D: The hospice circular requires a machine-specific CSR.
choice_analysis.E: The pharmacy must make that DEA determination.

related_facts: General Massachusetts ADD requirements also apply.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming hospice status relaxes machine-level controls.

reasoning_steps: Identify hospice acute-use ADD storage
Apply registration, monitoring, ownership, and reconciliation rules

questions.stem: A Massachusetts inpatient hospice has 18 licensed beds. What is the maximum number of Schedule II-V analgesic units permitted in its acute-use ADD under the current circular?

choices.text: A maximum stock of 40 analgesic units
A maximum stock of 60 analgesic units
A maximum stock of 75 analgesic units
A maximum stock of 100 analgesic units
A maximum stock of 150 analgesic units

choice_analysis.B: Sixty is the sedative/anticonvulsant cap in this bed tier, not the analgesic cap.
choice_analysis.C: Seventy-five is not the analgesic maximum for the 11-20-bed tier.
choice_analysis.D: An inpatient hospice with 11-20 beds may stock up to 100 Schedule II-V analgesic units in the acute-use ADD.
choice_analysis.E: One hundred fifty is the analgesic cap for the larger bed-capacity tier, not this hospice.

related_facts: Sedative/anticonvulsant and Schedule VI ancillary categories have separate caps.

reasoning_steps: Place 18 beds in the 11-20 tier
Apply the analgesic category maximum

questions.stem: A community pharmacy receives by fax an otherwise valid Schedule II prescription for a routine ambulatory patient. The patient is not in an LTCF or hospice and the drug is not a qualifying narcotic compounded for direct parenteral or infusion use. May the fax itself serve as the original Schedule II prescription?

choices.text: Yes, every faxed Schedule II prescription is an original once a pharmacist receives it.
Yes, if the prescriber calls afterward to confirm the fax.
No; absent a federal fax-as-original exception, the fax does not itself replace the required original prescription.
No, because Schedule II prescriptions may never be transmitted by fax for any purpose.
Yes, if the quantity is a seven-day supply or less.

explanation.core_reasoning: A routine Schedule II fax does not serve as the original unless a specific federal exception applies.

choice_analysis.A: Federal law has limited fax-as-original exceptions.
choice_analysis.B: A confirmation call does not create the stated exception.
choice_analysis.C: The ordinary fax is not the original.
choice_analysis.D: Federal law has defined exceptions and other fax uses.
choice_analysis.E: Quantity alone is not a fax-as-original exception.

related_facts: LTCF, hospice narcotic, and qualifying compounded narcotic prescriptions have separate exceptions.
explanation.mpje_trap: Treating fax transmission as equivalent to an electronic controlled-substance prescription.

reasoning_steps: Identify an ordinary Schedule II fax
Check whether any fax-as-original exception applies

questions.stem: A pharmacy serving a long-term-care facility receives a faxed Schedule II prescription for an LTCF resident. The prescription is otherwise valid. Which federal rule is most relevant to whether the fax may serve as the original?

choices.text: The fax can serve as the original for the Schedule II prescription to the LTCF resident under the specific federal exception.
The exception applies only if the Schedule II drug is a narcotic.
The fax is never an original because LTCF status affects only partial filling.
The fax becomes valid only after seven days have elapsed.
The facility must convert the prescription to Schedule III before the fax can be used.

explanation.core_reasoning: A faxed Schedule II prescription for an LTCF resident may serve as the original when federal requirements are met.

choice_analysis.A: Federal law provides an LTCF fax-as-original exception.
choice_analysis.B: The LTCF exception is not limited to narcotics.
choice_analysis.C: LTCF status also matters to this fax rule.
choice_analysis.D: No such waiting period applies.
choice_analysis.E: A facility cannot reclassify the drug.
